audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 is awarded to Swain at 7/10 while its own why says a Level 1 trade is 'almost always net-negative for you'. Levels 3, 6 and First item are all 'Skill' while their whys describe them as Swain's ownership windows. Packet chart reads Volibear/Skill/Swain/Skill/Swain/Swain/Swain. diff is 'HARD' while the final rating line says even at 52.69%.
audit.why: Four rows contradicted their own explanations, and diff contradicted every other difficulty statement on the page.
audit.corrected: Row 0 to Volibear (3/10), rows 2, 4 and 5 to Swain (7/10); win[] and phases[].side proposed as pairs. diff to EVEN.

audit.why: Four spikes present: Levels 2-3 root pattern, Level 6 Demonic Ascension, first item, and Volibear's Stormbringer dive window. Stormbringer is 160/135/110 s, which is what makes his level-6 spike a one-shot threat rather than a standing one.
audit.corrected: Stormbringer's rank-1 160 s cooldown added to spikes[3] so the dive window has a length.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] calls Frenzied Maul his passive. Frenzied Maul is his W; the passive is The Relentless Storm (attack speed then bonus magic damage). The healing is the second W cast on the same target. Also, Thundering Smash is an auto-attack reset — the stun lands on his next attack, not on the dash itself, and nothing in the text says so.
audit.why: Kit file is authority: W is Frenzied Maul with the heal on the repeat cast; Q is flagged autoReset and Riot's text says he stuns 'the first one he Attacks'. Reacting to the dash is one beat too late.
audit.corrected: wants.you[1] names Frenzied Maul as W and targets the second bite; dontsFull[0].d now gives the attack wind-up as the step-back cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere in this matchup — every line says 'when Thundering Smash is down' without ever saying how long that is.
audit.why: Thundering Smash is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, Sky Splitter a flat 16 s, Stormbringer 160/135/110. Those numbers turn vague respect into a countable window.
audit.corrected: Rank-1 numbers added to whys[1], whys[3] and spikes[3].text.

edits.before: E comes online but you are still mana-limited and he can Q-dash to close the gap before your root lands — test his reaction to W slow before committing a full combo.
edits.after: E comes online but you are mana-limited and Thundering Smash closes the gap in one dash — it is down 12 s at rank 1, so root his step-up only after he spends it.

edits.before: He may have Thundering Smash levelled but your W covers his entire approach path — trade only when R is soon available and keep the wave near your tower so he cannot chain his engage.
edits.after: Thundering Smash is his only gap-close and it is down 12 s — count it, then trade; keep the wave near your tower so his 16 s Sky Splitter shield cannot cover a second approach.

edits.before: Stormbringer disables your tower and opens a free-dive window — if Volibear hits 6 ahead of you, shove the wave and respect his all-in until you have R to answer.
edits.after: Stormbringer disables your tower and opens a free-dive window — it is a 160 s cooldown at rank 1, so once he spends it you own the next stretch of lane.

edits.before: Use W to slow him in the open and deny his passive Frenzied Maul proc on the minion wave
edits.after: Use W to slow him in the open and deny the second Frenzied Maul (W) bite that heals him

edits.before: That is Volibear's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: The stun lands on his next attack, not the dash — the wind-up is your step-back cue.

notes: Frenzied Maul was mislabelled as Volibear's passive; his passive is The Relentless Storm. Chart rows 0, 2, 4 and 5 flipped to match packet.levelChart, proposed as matched win[]/phases[].side pairs with ratings. Packet defect 'no cooldown-sequencing advice' addressed with rank-1 numbers for Q (12 s), E (16 s) and R (160 s).
